Account snapshot:
- Company: Ironwood Catalyst Solutions — mid-market product analytics SaaS (customer-facing insights + in-app guidance).
- Eng/Product team evaluating LLM features for agent and search; timeline accelerated by loss of previous vendor reliability.

History / recent timeline (shorthand):
- 2024-11-20: Intro call (Maya) — scoped use cases, initial ask: embeddings + chat for support agent. Agreed to run hosted API pilot.
- 2024-12-05: Hosted API demo (recording: ff_20241205_ironwood_demo). Good perf on short prompts; cost vs latency trade-offs discussed.
- 2025-01-10: POC kickoff for Dedicated (3-week POC): baseline model gpt-like-open-7b variant on Redwood hosted -> dedicated migration plan created.
- 2025-01-17: POC results review (ff_20250117_poc-review) — key metrics: 95th pct latency ~220ms for chat on dedicated pool; embedding throughput 120 req/sec; cost per 1M tokens ~ $80 (pooled).

Use-case & technical requirements (as stated by Ironwood):
- Primary: in-app conversational support assistant (multi-turn) + embeddings for semantic search across product docs.
- Latency target: p50 < 120ms for simple responses, p95 < 350ms for typical multi-turn flows.
- Throughput: steady-state 50-150 qps for embeddings-heavy queries during business hours; peak bursts up to 300 qps during product releases.
- Model preference: open-model family preferred (cost + licensing), Redwood-recommended 7B-13B variants ok.
- Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to cheaper/quantized variant on overload, with graceful degradation.

POC conclusions & performance notes:
- Dedicated pool met p95 latency SLA in controlled tests; slight variability when KV cache misses for long-context flows.
- Batching + prefix caching reduced token cost by ~18% vs naive calls.
- Need better SLO for cold cache/miss case; discussed pre-warming cache and warmup policy.

Pricing / packaging negotiation (current state):
- Redwood proposed three commit tiers for Dedicated (examples):
  * Silver: 250M tokens/month commit, 2x burst up to 500M for 72 hours, overage billed at 1.8x unit rate.
  * Gold: 500M tokens/month commit, 2.5x burst up to 1.25B for 48 hours, overage 1.5x unit rate.
  * Platinum: 1B tokens/month commit, 3x burst, lower unit price, 12-month ramp credit options.
- Ironwood preference: Gold tier initially, with ability to burst to Platinum capacity during quarterly releases.
- Key negotiation points raised by Ironwood: monthly commit flexibility during ramp, clear overage cap, reserved burst bank that auto-refills monthly, and credits during early months of ramp.
- Requested ramp schedule: 3-month ramp (25% month1, 50% month2, 100% month3) with pro-rated billing and reduced overage rates during ramp period.
- Legal: ask to add early-termination clause that allows them to scale down commit after 6 months with 60-day notice and no penalty if usage below 40% of commit.

Security & compliance notes:
- Require SOC2 attestations (provided), KMS integration for key wrap, and audit logging retention options. EU data residency must be guaranteed for some enterprise customers — Redwood asked to confirm region-specific routing.

Open questions / blockers (summary):
- Legal wording for SLA / IP & early-termination (legal reviewing now).
- Final overage rate and burst bank mechanics (finance needs modeled TCO vs current cloud infra).
- Confirmation of EU data residency and KMS HSM support.

Next steps (agreed):

- Contract & SOW review call scheduled with Ironwood legal on 2025-02-18.
- Tech kickoff for Dedicated onboarding once term sheet signed (target week of 2025-03-03).
